prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A developer/QA reference sheet: for each onboarding form field it gives the validation regex, a valid sample, and the message shown on failure — a lookup table read row by row while implementing or testing one field.","reading":"Readers arrive knowing the field name (or scan the Field column as an index), then move right to the pattern, check it against the example, and read the error copy. Comparison happens within a row, not down a column, so each row must read as a single unit and the Field column must stay a stable anchor; the regex is the densest, most consulted content and the error text is the only true prose.","groups":["col 1 Field is the row key and stands alone — it is the lookup handle and must remain visually distinct and unbroken","col 2 Pattern + col 3 Example valid form a spec pair: the rule and a value that satisfies it, read together and verified against each other","col 4 Error message is the outcome/consequence text, the only column of ordinary prose, and can wrap freely without losing meaning"],"keep_intact":["field identifiers such as account_email, postal_code_us, currency_amount, eu_vat_id (no mid-word breaks)","regex anchors and atoms: ^, $, \\d{7,14}, [A-Za-z0-9._!...], (?:-\\d{4})? — break only at |, (, [, { boundaries, never inside a character class or quantifier","example values such as an email address or 2024-01-15 (break at @ or - at worst)"],"may_wrap":["error-message sentences — natural prose, wraps at word spaces with no loss","long regex alternation/branch sequences — wrap between groups, not inside them","header labels 'Example valid' and 'Error message' over two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [147, 100, 55, 57] · table 360×3523px · row heights [106, 525, 571, 455, 408, 501, 548, 408] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 24 lines · mid-word splits 82
Design r0B: widths [120, 145, 45, 49] · table 360×4453px · row heights [129, 664, 804, 501, 455, 687, 641, 571] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 34 lines · mid-word splits 129
Design r0C: widths [150, 480, 120, 170] · table 921×919px · row heights [36, 153, 153, 106, 106, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 3 · OVERFLOWS the box by 561px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"Field column at 147px is the only one that works: account_email, postal_code_us, currency_amount and eu_vat_id all stay whole, and the row key is a stable left anchor. Total width respects the 360px box.","problems":"Unreadable as a reference sheet. The Pattern column collapses to 2–3 characters per line, so the regex is shattered into 24–34 line vertical ribbons; the Example column shows 'mira…or' stacked letter by letter and the Error column is a one-word-per-line column of prose. 82 mid-word splits means identifiers, atoms and quantifiers are cut mid-token — exactly the content the table exists to protect. 3523px of scrolling for 7 rows.","cause":"Widths [147,100,55,57] spend half the budget on Field, which needs only 126px of content, and starve the three columns that carry the actual data. Pattern needs ~1074px one-line and got 100; Example needs 167px for its longest token and got 55; Error prose needs ~180px to read and got 57. Total 985px, i.e. ~60px more scroll than r0C for the cleanest regex rendering and zero mid-word splits. Choose this if regex fidelity outranks scroll length."}]}
